title: DiffuDETR: Rethinking Detection Transformers with Denoising Diffusion Process
claim: Our method reaches higher accuracy than prior models at every training budget, with the largest gains over strong baselines.
layout: 1 panel, line and scatter plot, accuracy vs. training epochs, legend top-right
description: A single matplotlib-style plot with a light grid. The x-axis is training epochs (12, 24, 36, 50, 108, 500) and the y-axis is COCO val2017 AP (%), running from about 42 to 52. The two proposed methods, DiffuDINO and DiffuDETR, are drawn as bold red and crimson lines with triangle markers. DiffuDINO rises from about 47.5 to about 52. DiffuDETR rises from about 44.6 to about 50.2. The DINO baseline is a pink-purple star line, and DN-DETR is a blue line. Other baselines appear as isolated markers: DiffusionDet, DN-Deformable-DETR, Deformable-DETR, DAB-DETR, Faster-RCNN and Vanilla DETR. The legend at top right labels each one and marks ours with quotes. The eye goes first to the red lines at the top of the plot.
caption: Performance of DiffuDINO against other DETR and CNN-based models using ResNet-50 (He et al., 2016) backbone.
abstract: In this paper, we present DiffuDETR, a novel approach that formulates object detection as a conditional object query generation task, conditioned on the image and a set of noisy reference points. We integrate DETR-based models with denoising diffusion training to generate object queries' reference points from a prior gaussian distribution. We propose two variants: DiffuDETR, built on top of the Deformable DETR decoder, and DiffuDINO, based on DINO’s decoder with contrastive denoising queries (CDNs). To improve inference efficiency, we further introduce a lightweight sampling scheme that requires only multiple forward passes through the decoder. Our method demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple backbones and datasets, including COCO2017, LVIS, and V3Det, surpassing the performance of their respective baselines, with notable gains in complex and crowded scenes. Using ResNet-50 backbone we observe a +1.0 in COCO-val reaching 51.9 mAP on DiffuDINO compared to 50.9 mAP of the DINO. We also observe similar improvements on LVIS and V3DET datasets with +2.4 and +2.2 respectively. The code is available at https://github.com/MBadran2000/DiffuDETR.
